user_text: Plan a 1-day migration from SVN to Git for a small repo.
assistant_text:
# 1-Day SVN → Git Migration Plan

## Pre-Work (Night Before)
- [ ] Install `git-svn` or `svn2git`
- [ ] Audit SVN repo size and history depth
- [ ] Identify all branches/tags
- [ ] Collect SVN committer usernames

---

## Morning (2–3 hrs)

### 1. Create Authors File (30 min)
```bash
# Extract all SVN authors
svn log --quiet https://svn-repo/project | \
  grep "^r" | awk '{print $3}' | sort -u > authors.txt

# Format: svn_user = Full Name <email@example.com>
jdoe = John Doe <jdoe@company.com>
```

### 2. Clone SVN Repo (1–2 hrs)
```bash
git svn clone https://svn-repo/project \
  --authors-file=authors.txt \
  --stdlayout \          # assumes trunk/branches/tags
  --no-metadata \
  -s my-project
```
> ⚠️ Large histories can take longer — run overnight if needed.

---

## Midday (1–2 hrs)

### 3. Clean Up Branches & Tags
```bash
cd my-project

# Convert SVN tags to real Git tags
git for-each-ref refs/remotes/tags | cut -d / -f 5- | while read tag; do
  git tag "$tag" "refs/remotes/tags/$tag"
  git branch -r -d "tags/$tag"
done

# Convert remote branches to local
git for-each-ref refs/remotes | grep -v tags | cut -d / -f 4- | while read branch; do
  git branch "$branch" "refs/remotes/$branch"
  git branch -r -d "$branch"
done
```

### 4. Verify History
```bash
git log --oneline | head -20
git branch -a
git tag
```

---

## Afternoon (2 hrs)

### 5. Push to New Git Remote
```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/org/my-project.git
git push origin --all
git push origin --tags
```

### 6. Smoke Test Checklist
- [ ] Commit count matches SVN (`git log --oneline | wc -l`)
- [ ] All branches present
- [ ] All tags present
- [ ] Authors mapped correctly (no `(no author)`)
- [ ] Latest code matches SVN HEAD

---

## End of Day (1 hr)

### 7. Cutover
- [ ] Set SVN repo to **read-only**
- [ ] Update CI/CD pipelines to Git remote
- [ ] Notify team, share new clone URL
- [ ] Archive SVN repo URL in docs

---

## Quick Reference

| Tool | Best For |
|------|----------|
| `git svn` | Built-in, full control |
| `svn2git` | Cleaner wrapper around git-svn |
| Atlassian's importer | Bitbucket-hosted SVN |

---

**Total time estimate: 6–8 hrs** (mostly waiting on clone)

## Top 3 Migration Risks

### 1. 🕐 Clone Takes Too Long
Large histories or big binary files can make `git svn clone` run for **hours or days**, blowing the 1-day window.

**Mitigation:** Do a test clone with `--revision HEAD:HEAD` first to estimate speed. Run the full clone the night before.

---

### 2. 👤 Unmapped Authors
Any SVN committer missing from `authors.txt` will **crash the clone mid-way**.

**Mitigation:** Always run the author-extraction command first and double-check the file is complete before starting the clone.

---

### 3. 🌿 Mangled Branches/Tags
SVN's freeform structure means non-standard layouts (e.g., nested branches, typos in `/tags`) **won't convert cleanly**, leaving orphaned refs or missing history.

**Mitigation:** Audit `svn ls` on branches and tags before migrating. Handle edge cases manually post-clone.

## Migration Risk Checklist

- [ ] Test clone speed before migration day
- [ ] Verify `authors.txt` is complete — no missing committers
- [ ] Audit all branches and tags with `svn ls` beforehand
- [ ] Confirm no non-standard repo layout (`trunk/branches/tags`)
- [ ] Set SVN to read-only **before** final push to Git
Keep SVN read-write until the Git migration is fully verified — if anything fails, teams continue working in SVN as normal.
`git-svn` must be installed on the machine running the migration.

user_text: What is the fastest validation step?
assistant_text: Run `git log --oneline | wc -l` and compare the count against SVN's revision number — instant confirmation the full history migrated.
**Morning:** clone → **Midday:** clean branches/tags → **Afternoon:** push & verify → **EOD:** cut over and lock SVN.

assistant_text: The team lead or project owner.
Send a single team-wide message with the new Git repo URL and the exact time SVN goes read-only.
Clone with `git-svn`, clean up branches/tags, push to Git, validate history, get team lead approval, lock SVN, and notify the team — all in one day.

- Clone SVN repo with `git-svn`
- Clean branches and tags
- Push to Git remote
- Validate commit count
- Get team lead approval
- Lock SVN read-only
- Notify team with new URL
